Callanish Stones, Scotland

The Callanish Stones are an impressive stone circle, with rows of monoliths rising around 12 feet high in a cross-like formation. At its heart lies a chambered tomb, seemingly sheltered by the ancient stones.

Built by Neolithic people around 5,000 years ago, the site was used for rituals for at least a millennium. Its original purpose remains a mystery, though it may have served as an astronomical observatory or calendar.

Local legends speak of giants turned to stone and a magical cow. Unlike Stonehenge, Callanish is open to visitors who can walk among—and even touch—the stones.

Outlander fans may recognize the inspiration for the fictional Craigh na Dun. Visit in any season: summer sunshine and the Northern Lights each lend the stones their own kind of magic.
